parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional household survey with comparative analysis by geographic zone and community income cluster
parsed.population_and_sample: 540 households in 25 established slum or squatter settlements across the inner, middle, and outer zones of the Bangkok Metropolitan Region, surveyed in February–March 1994
parsed.exposure: Geographic zone and community income grouping, together with institutional and administrative service-delivery conditions such as municipal piped-water provision, waste-collection arrangements, service pricing, and community participation
parsed.outcome: Access to piped water and waste collection; water consumption, treatment, absolute cost and share of household income; waste-disposal practices; and demand or participation measures related to service improvement
parsed.rationale: The Household data section (pp. 275–276) reports a defined cross-sectional survey of 540 households and identifies the sampling, population, and measured service-access variables. Tables 4–5 and the Analysis/Synthesis sections (pp. 278–284) empirically compare piped-water access, water affordability, consumption, and waste services across geographic and income-defined communities. The Service delivery and Policy implications sections (pp. 274–285) explicitly connect these outcomes to municipal provision, pricing, agency capacity, and community-level governance mechanisms.
